# Generated page fields and capitalization

Original OPC/XML controls generated by `python tools/canvas_page_field_caps_fixture.py`; no third-party document engine or corpus content is used. Export each fixture to its matching `*-native.pdf` with the reference application, then run `python tools/record_page_field_caps_reference.py`. Reference fonts are named, not redistributed.

The reference application renders three two-page controls covering lower/upper Roman and lower alphabetic section numbering. Each header has normal, direct caps, direct small caps, paragraph-style caps and paragraph-style small caps rows. Each row includes simple and complex PAGE, locked simple and complex PAGE, locked NUMPAGES and locked SECTIONPAGES.

Observed behavior:

- Generated PAGE results keep the numbering format's case and the full run size, regardless of surrounding caps/smallCaps. Ordinary text still uses its capitalization.
- PAGE and NUMPAGES refresh in headers even when fldLock is true. The locked SECTIONPAGES result remains cached and retains capitalization.
- The preview applies these rules during page-story layout. Original run properties, cached field results, locks and package XML remain unchanged. Story editing remains unsupported.

This is a reference compatibility divergence from the general run capitalization and field-lock prose. It is keyed to field type and page-story context, never a template name. Unsupported field formats still use the existing fallback.

Sizing issue originally exposed by these controls: at 16pt, the reference application's Times New Roman small-cap letters export at approximately 13pt (12.96pt PDF value); the former fixed two-point reduction produced 14pt. The generic proportional rule and independent sizing controls in `../small-caps-sizes` now correct it. That separate sizing issue is not hidden by the tests: these controls assert case, refreshed/cached values, and full-size generated PAGE numerals, not full row width or complete font fidelity.
